standard_prerequisites.reference: Universal openness, base change, principal opens, polynomial extensions; no cited result replaces the retained argument
standard_prerequisites.use: Definition of a universally open morphism, base change of schemes, the principal opens D(g) as a basis, and the affine-space extension A^n x_S X. The two reductions are retained in full.

core_obligations: Reduce condition (3) implies (1) to the affine local statement about a ring map A -> B whose base change along some A-algebra A' fails to induce an open map of spectra.

Choose g in B' with non-open image, rewrite it as sum a'_i tensor b_i, and obtain the contradiction from the cartesian square involving B[x_1,...,x_n] and the surjectivity of D(h) onto a quasi-compact open.

proof_roadmap.step: Record the easy implications (1) implies (2) implies (3), then reduce the converse to affine opens V in S, U in X, W in T where U x_V W -> W is not open.
Work with a ring map A -> B failing openness after base change, isolate g in B', set h = sum x_i b_i, and derive the contradiction from the cartesian square of polynomial algebras.

difficulty_reason: Three conditions are shown equivalent, and the only hard implication is (3) implies (1): openness is a local-on-the-source, local-on-the-base property that must be recovered from the special base changes A^n x X -> A^n x S alone. The proof performs two reductions. First it descends to affine opens where the failed base change has a non-open image, reducing to a statement about a ring map A -> B whose base change along some A-algebra A' is not open. Then it uses that principal opens are a basis to isolate a single g in B', writes g as sum a'_i tensor b_i, forms h = sum x_i b_i in B[x_1,...,x_n], and derives a contradiction from the cartesian square of polynomial algebras. The engineering difficulty is that the polynomial variables must be introduced only after the pathological g is known, and the contradiction relies on the surjectivity of D(h) onto a quasi-compact open. Retained author proof at lines 21739-21785.
